guidance.procedure: Evaluate breadth, identification, and oral form independently. Reconstruct every operative route into the protected class, including split continuations and repeated definitions. Technical-only coverage requires a closed class confined to technical matter; business, financial, commercial, customer, personnel, marketing, or other coverage opposes exclusivity. Universal express identification requires every route to depend on marking or designation; nature, context, reasonable-expectation, or presumed-confidential routes oppose it. Oral material qualifies when spoken disclosure can enter the class, even subject to designation or later confirmation. Cite all fragments creating the responsive route or condition, including illustrative categories when they establish breadth, but exclude headings, exclusions, and unrelated neighboring routes.

Maintain three separate lifecycle ledgers. For return or destruction, identify the operative command, its full object, and the exact trigger: termination or expiration is responsive, while request, completion, or ended discussions alone is not. For retention, inspect that command together with every express archival, backup, legal-compliance, dispute, professional-record, or inaccessible-copy exception; an express retained-copy exception permits some possession, while an unconditional all-material-and-copies command supports the opposed boundary. For survival, require confidentiality or use obligations expressly continuing after termination, not a fixed term, ownership rule, disposition duty, or unrelated restriction. Cite only the complete fragments for the ledger being answered and do not transfer evidence among the three tests.

Decide outsider disclosure, employee disclosure, and copying separately. For each, match the receiving actor, regulated action, exact recipient or object class, quantifier, and attached conditions. Employee-only access does not establish permission for consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other outsiders; outsider permission does not automatically establish employee access. A direct prohibition covering the queried class can support the restrictive boundary, but silence or discretionary written consent alone cannot. For copying, a purpose- or necessity-limited exception permits some copies, while an absolute or consent-only prohibition opposes that permission. Cite every independently operative rule and the fragments supplying need-to-know, authorization, confidentiality, or purpose conditions; exclude use limits, safeguards, liability, notice, and adjacent recipient classes.

Start with the operative exclusion or permission lead-in, then follow only the responsive continuation. Independent development must concern development without using, referring to, relying on, or accessing protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; independent development, prior possession, public availability, employee access, and descriptive definition text are not substitutes. Treat compelled-disclosure authority and notice as separate propositions: verify legal compulsion, an actual notice duty or express excuse, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. A heading or compelled-disclosure permission alone does not establish notice. Cite the lead-in when it supplies scope and every continuation completing the responsive exception; exclude neighboring exceptions even when grammatically adjacent. If the matching exception is absent, do not infer its opposite.

Run separate searches for the exact regulated conduct. Reverse engineering requires an express ban on reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, decrypting, reconstructing, re-identifying, or materially equivalent analysis of protected material or an embodying product; confidentiality, copying, ownership, return, no-license, signature, and severability clauses are not substitutes. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct aimed at the specified representatives. Restrictions concerning customers, business opportunities, leads, transactions, ordinary contact, competition, or standstill conduct do not establish representative solicitation. Match actor, modality, object or people, duration, and exceptions. If the direct conduct is absent, use absence rather than inventing an opposing permission; cite only the complete operative chain.

Test rights and agreement secrecy separately. No-license requires operative language that no license, right, title, interest, option, or other right is granted or implied; ownership, restricted use, access, or a disclaimer alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of the agreement's existence or terms, or of the fact, status, or substance of negotiations or discussions; an entire-agreement clause or ordinary confidentiality of disclosed information is not responsive. Cite every fragment carrying the protected subject and prohibition, excluding headings, signatures, purpose clauses, and neighboring ownership or use text.

Locate every independently operative provision regulating the receiving actor's use of protected information. Match the actor, protected object, permitted purpose, prohibition on other purposes, and each exception or qualification that narrows the permission. A recital explaining why information is exchanged, a disclosure authorization, confidentiality duty, copying rule, ownership statement, or no-license clause is not itself a use restriction. Cite all independently responsive operative repetitions and qualifications, even when one clause is sufficient; include a separate purpose definition only when the operative restriction incorporates it and the definition supplies the responsive purpose. Exclude neighboring agreement-secrecy, recipient-class, and intellectual-property language that imposes no use condition.

Resolve three propositions independently. For technical-only scope, reconstruct every operative admission route into the protected class; any route covering business, financial, customer, marketing, personnel, commercial, or other nontechnical material opposes exclusivity. For universal express identification, ask whether every route requires the discloser’s marking or designation; a nature-, context-, reasonable-expectation-, or automatically confidential route opposes universality. For oral coverage, require a route admitting spoken or visual disclosure, even if designation or later confirmation is required. Cite the complete split definition for the proposition tested, including incorporated conditions, but do not transfer a fragment responsive only to another proposition.

complete_original_evidence_texts: 1. Confidential Information means:

(i) technologies in written or tangible form disclosed to COMPANY from time to time after the Effective Date of this Agreement by ROCHESTER and identified with particularity at time of disclosure and marked confidential; and

(ii) technologies communicated orally or visually to COMPANY by ROCHESTER, if it is reduced to writing or other tangible form by ROCHESTER on or before the date thirty days after the date of such communication, marked confidential, and promptly delivered to COMPANY.

Confidential information also includes any information of the owner and a third party with which the Owner deals, including, but not limited to: financial information, business records, plans, trade secrets, product ideas, technical data of any type, contracts, billing records, pricing structure, discounts, property, investments, strategic alliances, partnerships, customer or client lists.
The nature of the information and manner of the disclosure are such that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.
